title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: The Swell Roars Back: Broad Rally Wipes Away Tech Jitters
conditions.summary: Stocks ripped higher across the board as oil slid and chip stocks rebounded from last week's selloff, with all 11 sectors green and small caps leading. Nvidia fell on a board review of its CEO, but it couldn't stop the wave.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: S&P 500 rose 2.35% to 7,549.94, clawing back from its worst week since April 2025.
Nasdaq Composite jumped 2.74% to 25,253.14; the Dow added 1,104 points (+2.15%) to 52,389.75.
Russell 2000 led with a 3.15% gain to 2,840.81, showing the buying went well beyond megacap tech.
Lower oil prices and a rebound in AI and chip stocks after last week's tech selloff drove the rally.
All 11 S&P sectors finished green, led by industrials (+4.6%); energy faded to about flat.
Breadth was strong: roughly 75% of stocks rose. The S&P opened up about 0.9% and built gains all day.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: No major US economic data or Fed speakers today; September wholesale inventories were the only release.
US crude fell about 4.3% to near $87 a barrel on hopes for US-Iran talks, though officials said no breakthrough is near.
The 10-year Treasury yield edged up about 2 basis points to 4.88%.
VIX dropped about 22% to 20.08; gold rose about 1.8% to roughly $4,149; bitcoin gained about 1.3% to near $74,950.
The Fed held rates at 3.75%-4.00% in October, and futures lean toward a December hike, putting Tuesday's CPI in focus.
Citi strategists cut US stocks and tech to neutral and shifted toward Europe.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: CEG (Constellation Energy): +10%+ — beat earnings estimates and raised full-year guidance.
AMD (Advanced Micro Devices): about +12% midday — Oppenheimer upgraded it to Outperform.
NET (Cloudflare): almost +10% — investors piled back into AI infrastructure names.
TSLA (Tesla): +5.5% — robotaxi service expanding to more cities.
GFR (Greenfire Resources): about +38% — agreed to be bought by Strathcona Resources.
NVDA (Nvidia): -4.3% — board opened an independent review of reports involving CEO Jensen Huang.
IONS (Ionis Pharmaceuticals): about -25% — cut its 2026 Tryngolza sales forecast roughly in half.
HIMS (Hims & Hers): about -12% — slid ahead of its earnings report.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Before the open: Constellation Energy beat and raised guidance, closing up more than 10%.
After the close: Hims & Hers missed on EPS and guided Q4 revenue to $875M-$895M, below the roughly $953M expected.
Lucid reported a Q3 miss on both revenue and earnings.
Hyperfine beat on EPS (-$0.06 vs -$0.08 expected) and rose about 8% after hours.
Also reporting after the bell: Rocket Lab, Occidental Petroleum, Take-Two, Plug Power and The Trade Desk.

sections.title: Business News
items: Nvidia's independent directors are reviewing reports about CEO Jensen Huang; the board says it has full confidence in him.
Strathcona Resources agreed to acquire Greenfire Resources for C$11.00 cash or 0.25 Strathcona shares per share.
NRG Energy agreed to sell six gas plants to LS Power for $4 billion in cash.
Fervo Energy's first Cape Station geothermal unit entered commercial operation; it has a 396 MW deal with Google.
Surgery Partners rose after HealthSpan Partners raised its cash offer amid a rival bid.

sections.title: On Deck
items: 7:30 AM CT: October CPI — consensus +0.3% m/m headline, +0.2% m/m core.
Before the open: Sea Limited reports earnings.
After the close: CoreWeave reports (consensus loss of $1.45 per share).
Fed speakers: Governor Christopher Waller and Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman on the economic outlook.

script_source:
Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Monday, November ninth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is melting into the water, and we got one sweet last set to close out the day. Gus the wonder dog spent the afternoon chasing sandpipers, and his tail is still going. Give the crew a sunset hello, Gus! [BARK]

Let's start with the final set. After last week's gnarly tech wipeout, the swell roared back. The S and P five hundred jumped two point three five percent to close near seven thousand five hundred fifty. The Nasdaq Composite surged two point seven four percent to about twenty-five thousand two hundred fifty. The Dow climbed one thousand one hundred four points, or two point one five percent, to about fifty-two thousand three hundred ninety. And the small caps in the Russell two thousand led the lineup, up about three point one five percent. All eleven sectors finished green, and about three out of four stocks rose. That's a big, glassy wave.

Now the wind and weather. The big tailwind was oil. U S crude fell more than four percent to about eighty-seven dollars a barrel, on hopes for U S and Iran talks. The fear gauge, the V I X, dropped more than twenty-one percent to about twenty. The ten-year Treasury yield edged up two basis points to four point eight eight percent. Gold gained almost two percent, and bitcoin rose about one percent. No major data or Fed speakers today, but traders see a strong chance of a December rate hike, so tomorrow's inflation report matters.

Here's the lineup. Nvidia was the one paddling against the current, down more than four percent, after its board opened a review of reports involving chief executive Jensen Huang. Other chip names were stoked. A M D jumped about twelve percent midday after an upgrade from Oppenheimer, and Broadcom rose about eight percent. Tesla gained more than five percent as its robotaxis rolled into more cities. Ionis Pharmaceuticals wiped out, down about a quarter, after halving a key sales forecast. And Constellation Energy beat earnings, raised its outlook, and hung ten all the way to the sand, up more than ten percent. Gus, that ride earns you a treat! Catch it, buddy! [SNACK]

Over on the tide chart. Constellation reported before the bell. After the close, Hims and Hers missed on profit and guided below forecasts, after falling almost twelve percent today. Lucid missed on both sales and profit. Hyperfine, a little grom in medical imaging, beat and rose about eight percent after hours.

Beach talk. Strathcona Resources agreed to buy Greenfire Resources, and Greenfire popped about thirty-eight percent. N R G Energy agreed to sell six gas plants for four billion dollars in cash. And strategists at Citi cut U S stocks and tech to neutral. One great set doesn't make a season.

Tomorrow's forecast. The October consumer price index lands at seven thirty A M Central. Forecasters expect three tenths of a percent for the month, and two tenths for core. Sea Limited reports before the open, and CoreWeave reports after the close. Fed Governor Christopher Waller and Vice Chair Michelle Bowman are both scheduled to speak.

So wax your board tonight, and catch the Dawn Patrol tomorrow morning for the inflation reaction. Want a call on a stock, E T F or futures contract? Type it into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
